step1_analysis.circuit_type: Half-Rate Binary Phase Detector (CML XNOR Gate)
step1_analysis.description: A current-mode logic (CML) XNOR gate utilized as a half-rate phase detector. It compares a differential clock signal with a differential data signal to produce an output whose average voltage is proportional to the phase difference. Note: XM3 appears to have a shorted gate/source in the extracted netlist, which makes it act as an asymmetric gate, but it still performs the phase detection function by choking the tail current on one state.

paper_reference.title: A 10-Gb/s CMOS Clock and Data Recovery Circuit With a Half-Rate Binary Phase/Frequency Detector

paper_reported.value: Not explicitly reported for this sub-block

sky130_expected.calculation: With a ~1.2mA tail current (determined by a 600 ohm tail resistor) and 500 ohm effective pull-up resistance, the voltage drop is 1.2mA * 500 ohm = 0.6V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard CML logic swing to keep transistors in saturation while providing enough noise margin.

v_avg.description: Average output voltage at 90-degree phase shift

sky130_expected.calculation: At 90 degrees phase shift, the XNOR output is low (~1.2V) 50% of the time and high (1.8V) 50% of the time. Average = (1.8 + 1.2) / 2 = 1.5V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The average voltage serves as the phase detector output to the loop filter.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the RC time constant at the output node. R=500 ohm, C_parasitic ~ 50fF -> tau = 25ps. t_rise ~ 2.2 * tau = 55ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Fast rise time is required for high-speed operation.

power.description: Power consumption of the phase detector core

sky130_expected.reasoning: A single CML gate consumes a small fraction of the total CDR power.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure the phase detector's output swing, average voltage (gain), rise/fall times, and power consumption at 1 GHz with a 90-degree phase shift.
step3_testbench.spice:
* CML XNOR Phase Detector Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
* Using a tail resistor instead of ideal current source to prevent negative infinity voltages when the asymmetric path is blocked
R_tail N3 0 600

* Output load resistors
R_out1 VDD N0 1k
R_out2 VDD N2 1k
* Short outputs together for XNOR function
R_short N0 N2 1m

* Inputs (1 GHz, 1ns period)
* Clock inputs
VCLK LABEL_NET_3 0 PULSE(0.6 1.2 0 50p 50p 400p 1n)
VCLK_B LABEL_NET_5 0 PULSE(1.2 0.6 0 50p 50p 400p 1n)

* Data inputs (90 degree phase shift = 250ps delay)
VDATA LABEL_NET_0 0 PULSE(0.6 1.2 250p 50p 50p 400p 1n)
VDATA_B LABEL_NET_4 0 PULSE(1.2 0.6 250p 50p 50p 400p 1n)
VLABEL_NET_1 LABEL_NET_1 0 PULSE(0.6 1.2 250p 50p 50p 400p 1n)

* DUT
XM1 N0 LABEL_NET_0 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 VDD LABEL_NET_1 N4 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 VDD N1 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N1 LABEL_NET_3 N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N2 LABEL_NET_4 N4 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N4 LABEL_NET_5 N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}

.control
  tran 5p 5n
  
  meas tran v_max max v(N0) from=2n to=5n
  meas tran v_min min v(N0) from=2n to=5n
  let v_swing = v_max - v_min
  print v_swing
  
  meas tran v_avg avg v(N0) from=2n to=5n
  
  * Measure rise and fall times
  meas tran t_rise trig v(N0) val=1.4 rise=2 targ v(N0) val=1.7 rise=2
  meas tran t_fall trig v(N0) val=1.7 fall=2 targ v(N0) val=1.4 fall=2
  
  op
  let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
  print power
  
  quit
.endc
